issues.sym: Rough or delayed shifts, humming or scraping noises, flaring revs, or the van suddenly losing drive. Failures can come with little warning.
issues.why: The 4-speed automatic in the first-generation van works hard moving a heavy, loaded body, and skipped fluid changes speed up wear. Transmission failure is the most reported problem for these years, often between about 50,000 and 110,000 miles.
issues.next: If it is shifting badly, check the fluid level and condition and look for leaks near the front axles. Have a transmission shop diagnose it before it fails completely; a rebuilt or used transmission is the usual fix.

issues.t: Overheating at idle from fan or water pump failure
issues.sym: The temperature gauge climbs when idling or in traffic, the A/C stops cooling at idle, or you hear a squeal or see coolant drips at the front of the engine.
issues.why: The electric radiator fans can fail, so the engine gets hot when there's no airflow. Owners also report water pump, belt idler pulley and radiator failures on these vans.
issues.next: Watch the gauge and turn off the A/C if it climbs. Check that both fans run when the engine is hot, and have leaks and the belt pulleys checked before they strand you.

issues.sym: Bubbling paint or rust along the bottom inner edges of the doors, especially the rear and sliding doors.
issues.why: Water and road salt collect along the lower door seams of the first-generation van, and work vans often have chipped paint that lets rust start.
issues.next: Wash out the door drain holes and touch up chips early. Have rust treated before it spreads through the panel.

issues.t: Hood release or hood lock seized
issues.sym: The hood won't open with the key or the release, or the latch sticks.
issues.why: The hood on these vans opens with a key lock in the grille, and the lock cylinder and latch can corrode, especially in snowy, salted climates.
issues.next: Clean and lubricate the hood lock and latch every year. If it's already stuck, a shop can release it and replace the latch or lock.

issues.t: Door locks or cargo door lock stop working
issues.sym: One or more doors, often the rear cargo doors, won't lock or unlock with the remote or switch, or the key fob stops working.
issues.why: Door lock actuators, latches and switches wear out from heavy daily use on work vans.
issues.next: Test every door with the remote, the switch and the key. A failed lock actuator is replaced at the door.

issues.sym: The paint peels, flakes off or wears through in patches.
issues.why: Paint durability on the first-generation van is a known weak spot.
issues.next: Touch up or repaint bare areas soon so rust doesn't start.

issues.sym: The cruise control won't turn on or won't hold speed.
issues.why: Common causes are a blown fuse, a faulty brake pedal switch, or an engine fault code that disables cruise; a bad engine computer is rarer.
issues.next: Check that the brake lights work and look at the cruise fuses. Have the codes read even if the check engine light is off.

issues.sym: Water on the floor or seats after rain, sometimes in large amounts.
issues.why: Owners of early vans report major water leaks, typically from door or body seals.
issues.next: Find the source with a water test and reseal it promptly to avoid rust, mold and electrical problems.

issues.sym: No symptoms; the clips matter for head protection in a crash.
issues.why: On 2010 vans built through May 2010, the push pins holding the headliner above the side pillar trim did not meet head-impact standards.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. The dealer replaces the pins for free.

issues.sym: The wipers leave streaks or one wiper arm comes off the van, leaving the windshield uncleared.
issues.why: The wiper arms on some 2011-2012 vans were not riveted properly.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. The dealer replaces both wiper arms and blades for free.

issues.sym: Long cracks start near the bottom edge of the windshield without an obvious impact.
issues.why: Owners of 2011 vans report cracks spreading from the lower edge of the glass at low mileage, suggesting stress where the glass meets the body.
issues.next: Have the glass replaced before the crack spreads into your view. Ask if the original installation or body seal was at fault.

issues.sym: Harsh or erratic shifts, slipping, getting stuck in one gear, rolling back on hills, or the van suddenly losing drive at a stop.
issues.why: The 8-speed automatic used from 2019 can suffer internal failure, solenoid faults and fluid leaks. Owners report failures mostly between about 65,000 and 90,000 miles, and replacement is one of the biggest repairs on this vehicle.
issues.next: Have codes read as soon as shifting changes. Check fluid for leaks, and ask a Ford dealer about software updates, bulletins and any extended coverage for your VIN before paying for a transmission.

issues.sym: The shifter doesn't put the van in the chosen gear, the gear display doesn't match, or the van rolls after you select Park.
issues.why: The bushing that connects the shift cable to the transmission can wear out or fall off. Ford recalled vans with the 2.5L engine and 6-speed automatic, then expanded the recall.
issues.next: Use the parking brake every time until it's fixed. Check your VIN; the dealer replaces the bushing and adds a protective cap for free.

issues.sym: You keep topping up coolant but see no leak, then get a high temperature warning, misfires, white exhaust smoke or a check engine light.
issues.why: The 1.6L EcoBoost can let coolant seep into the cylinders through the head gasket area. Low coolant can then overheat the engine and crack the cylinder head, which can leak oil onto hot parts.
issues.next: Check the coolant reservoir weekly and don't drive if the temperature warning comes on. Have a cooling system pressure test and a cylinder leak test done if coolant keeps disappearing.

issues.t: Low coolant can crack cylinder head (recall)
issues.sym: An engine overheat warning, loss of power or smoke from the engine bay after coolant runs low.
issues.why: Ford recalled 1.6L EcoBoost vans because driving with low coolant can overheat and crack the cylinder head, and leaking oil could start a fire. The fix adds a coolant level sensor and warning.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. The dealer installs the coolant level sensor and software for free.

issues.t: Engine overheat protection set too late (recall)
issues.sym: Engine overheating, a temperature warning, and possible engine damage or fire after a coolant leak.
issues.why: Engine computer software on 2.5L vans had fail-safe temperature limits set too high, so it waited too long to protect the engine when coolant was lost. Ford issued the update in 2020 and recalled again in 2025 because some updates were done incorrectly.
issues.next: Check your VIN for both recalls even if the first update was done. The fix is a free software update.

issues.sym: Transmission fluid leaks, loss of drive or warning lights.
issues.why: The bolts on the start/stop accumulator end cap on some 2019-2020 vans may be loose or missing, letting transmission fluid leak out, which can cause loss of drive or a fire.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. The dealer replaces the accumulator for free.

issues.t: Door may not latch or may open while driving (recall)
issues.sym: A door won't latch, bounces back open, or looks closed but isn't, and could open while driving.
issues.why: Parts inside the side door latches can break. Ford recalled these vans in 2016, again in 2020 because some repairs weren't done right, and in 2023 for cracking front door latch pawls.
issues.next: Check your VIN for all open door latch recalls. Dealers check and replace the latches for free.

issues.t: Panoramic roof panel may come loose (recall)
issues.sym: Wind noise or water leaks around the fixed glass roof, and in rare cases the roof panel separating from the van while driving.
issues.why: On passenger vans with the panoramic Vista roof, the bond between the roof panel and the body may be weak. Ford ran several recalls covering 2014-2019 vans.
issues.next: Check your VIN for all roof recalls. Dealers remove, clean and rebond the roof panel for free.

issues.t: Backup camera image blank or distorted (recall)
issues.sym: The rear camera picture is fuzzy, upside down, flickering or blank, or it stays on the screen after you leave reverse.
issues.why: Ford recalled 2015-2018 vans for failing rearview cameras and 2018-2022 vans for camera software errors.
issues.next: Use your mirrors and check your VIN for open camera recalls. Dealers replace the camera or update the software for free.

issues.t: Fuel pump can fail and stall the van (recall)
issues.sym: The engine sputters, stalls while driving or won't restart.
issues.why: Some fuel pumps on vans built from November 2013 to August 2014 had poor nickel plating that can make the pump fail.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check your VIN for this recall. The dealer replaces the fuel pump for free.

issues.sym: No warning before failure; the outer panel of the sliding door could come off while driving.
issues.why: On some 2014 cargo vans the sliding door panel was not bonded strongly enough.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. The dealer rebonds the panel for free.

issues.t: Fuel lines can rub and leak (recall)
issues.sym: A fuel smell or visible fuel leak under the van.
issues.why: On 2014 vans built through July 2014 the fuel and vapor lines could touch and wear through, risking a fuel leak and fire.
issues.next: If you smell fuel, don't drive it. Check your VIN; dealers reroute or replace the lines for free.

issues.sym: The gauges and warning lights stop working, and warning chimes may not sound.
issues.why: A software mismatch could shut down the instrument cluster on vans built from May 2014 to July 2015.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: you may not see your speed or warning lights, so ease off, keep a safe distance, and pull over where it's safe. Restarting the car once parked may bring the display back; if it doesn't, have it fixed before you drive again. Check your VIN for this recall. The dealer updates the cluster software for free.

issues.sym: ABS or stability control warning lights, and reduced stability control.
issues.why: On some 2016 vans built from February to June 2016, the brake hydraulic pump may contain metal debris.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. The dealer replaces the pump for free.

issues.t: Seat belt pretensioners may not fire (recall)
issues.sym: No symptoms; the front seat belt tighteners might not work in a crash.
issues.why: The front seat belt pretensioners on some 2016-2017 vans may have an incorrect propellant mix.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. The dealer replaces the seat belt assemblies for free.

issues.sym: No symptoms; the problem would only show in a crash.
issues.why: Some driver or passenger front airbag modules were built without part of their inflator propellant.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. The dealer replaces the airbag module for free.

issues.sym: No symptoms; the windshield could come out in a crash.
issues.why: Some 2016 and 2020 vans may have windshields without enough adhesive bonding to the body.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. The dealer inspects and rebonds the windshield for free.

issues.t: Passenger seat belt won't hold child seat (recall)
issues.sym: The front passenger belt's locking mode may switch off early, so a child seat may not stay tight.
issues.why: The automatic locking retractor on the front passenger belt of some 2021 vans can deactivate too soon.
issues.next: Don't use a child seat in front until fixed. Check your VIN; the dealer replaces the belt for free.

issues.t: Water dripping into front passenger footwell
issues.sym: Wet carpet or water dripping onto the front passenger floor, especially after rain or with the A/C on.
issues.why: Ford issued bulletins for 2014-2020 Transit Connect vans with water dripping into the passenger footwell.
issues.next: Ask a Ford dealer to check the bulletin for your VIN. Dry the carpet promptly to prevent mold and electrical problems.

issues.sym: The battery is dead after the van sits overnight or for a few days.
issues.why: Ford issued a service message for 2014-2017 Transit Connect vans with a condition that drains the battery while parked.
issues.next: Have the battery tested and ask a dealer to check the battery drain service message. Aftermarket upfit wiring can also cause drains.

issues.t: Gear indicator shows the wrong position
issues.sym: The gear display doesn't match where the shifter is.
issues.why: Ford issued several bulletins for incorrect shifter position display on 2014-2021 Transit Connect and other models.
issues.next: Make sure the van is really in Park before getting out. Have a dealer check the bulletin, and also check the shifter bushing recall.

issues.t: Check engine light with cam timing codes
issues.sym: A check engine light with camshaft timing codes, sometimes with a rough idle.
issues.why: Debris can stick the variable cam timing solenoid. Ford issued service messages for these codes across many 2015-2021 models.
issues.next: Have the codes read and keep up with oil changes. Replacing the solenoid is a modest repair.

issues.t: Remote start shuts engine off right away
issues.sym: The engine starts with remote start and then shuts off immediately.
issues.why: Ford released service messages for 2016-2018 Transit Connect vans where remote start causes an immediate shutoff.
issues.next: Start the van with the key while waiting for a dealer to apply the fix.

issues.sym: The center screen goes black or blue, freezes or doesn't respond to touch.
issues.why: Ford issued many service messages for SYNC 3 screen and software problems on these vans.
issues.next: Restart the system and install the latest SYNC update. A dealer can reflash it if needed.
